is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. (An. gambiae s.s. and An. arabiensis) as malaria vectors in Benin.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (1014F), Vgsc L995S (1014S), and Ace-1 G280S (G119S) in Table 1.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 provides detailed genotype counts (Leu-Leu, Leu-Phe, Leu-Ser, Phe-Phe, Ser-Ser) for various populations and time points.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from four field sites in Benin (Cotonou, Tori-Bossito, Bohicon, Malanville) between 2008 and 2010.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical field study reporting original data on insecticide resistance and marker frequencies.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies four sentinel sites: Cotonou, Tori-Bossito, Bohicon, and Malanville.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study covers a collection period from October 2008 to June 2010, which is within a 3-year window.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a new, specific longitudinal monitoring program conducted by the authors.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including genotype counts and site information, are provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study monitored insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.l. populations in four sites in Benin from 2008 to 2010. It reports high levels of DDT and pyrethroid resistance, associated with the L1014F and L1014S kdr mutations and metabolic mechanisms. It provides the first evidence of the L1014S mutation in An. arabiensis in Benin.
